components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. It is then stored and returned in that E.164 form (e.g.
            '0412 345 678' becomes '+61412345678'). A value that cannot form
            valid E.164 is rejected with 400.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create the server sets it to its current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address (i.e. they share a household).
            Write-only; it is not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner

## Summary

I implemented the GOLD membership tier rule: an owner's `membershipTier` is `'GOLD'` when their household (owners sharing the same `householdId`) has 3+ members after the create; otherwise the existing SILVER/BRONZE rules still apply.

Changes, following the existing "fixed at creation time" idiom used for the other derived owner fields:

1. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a persisted `householdSize` field (`household_size` column) with getter/setter.

2. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, after the household-id assignment, record the household size: `householdMembers.size() + 1` when the owner joins a shared household (non-null `householdId`), otherwise `1`. This is fixed at creation time, matching `namesakeCount`, `customerCode`, etc.

3. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — updated the `membershipTier` expression to return `GOLD` when `householdSize >= 3`, else fall through to the existing SILVER/BRONZE derivation (so SILVER/BRONZE remain dynamically derived from `namesakeCount`/`email` as before).

4. **`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `household_size` column to the `owners` table in all four schemas.

5. **`openapi.yml`** — updated the `membershipTier` description to document the GOLD rule.

The `AcceptanceTest.coreGoldForThreeMemberHousehold` test passes, and the full suite builds green.

I chose the fixed-at-create approach (storing the size) over re-deriving it at read time deliberately: the spec says "after **this** create," so the third member is GOLD while the first two — whose households had only 1 and 2 members at their own create time — correctly are not, even though all three now share the household.

I implemented the GOLD membership tier rule: an owner's `membershipTier` is `'GOLD'` when their household (owners sharing the same `householdId`) has 3+ members after the create; otherwise the existing SILVER/BRONZE rules still apply.

Changes, following the existing "fixed at creation time" idiom used for the other derived owner fields:

1. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a persisted `householdSize` field (`household_size` column) with getter/setter.

2. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, after the household-id assignment, record the household size: `householdMembers.size() + 1` when the owner joins a shared household (non-null `householdId`), otherwise `1`. This is fixed at creation time, matching `namesakeCount`, `customerCode`, etc.

3. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — updated the `membershipTier` expression to return `GOLD` when `householdSize >= 3`, else fall through to the existing SILVER/BRONZE derivation (so SILVER/BRONZE remain dynamically derived from `namesakeCount`/`email` as before).

4. **`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `household_size` column to the `owners` table in all four schemas.

5. **`openapi.yml`** — updated the `membershipTier` description to document the GOLD rule.

The `AcceptanceTest.coreGoldForThreeMemberHousehold` test passes, and the full suite builds green.

I chose the fixed-at-create approach (storing the size) over re-deriving it at read time deliberately: the spec says "after **this** create," so the third member is GOLD while the first two — whose households had only 1 and 2 members at their own create time — correctly are not, even though all three now share the household.
